episode.observableAction: Mid-afternoon light comes through the small apartment window as the subject sits on the floor near a low table, trying to tie the laces of a worn sneaker before going out. The laces are uneven and the knot keeps slipping loose. The caregiver, already wearing a jacket and standing by the door with a cloth shopping bag, glances at the clock, walks over, and kneels beside the subject. Without asking anything, the caregiver gently moves the subject’s hands aside, straightens the shoe on the subject’s foot, pulls the laces tight, and quickly forms a secure double knot. The caregiver pats the tied shoe once, stands up, and gestures toward the doorway for the subject to follow so they can leave the apartment.

Late morning in the apartment, the caregiver stands at the small kitchen counter with a plastic basin of washed vegetables and a cloth shopping bag open on a chair. The caregiver calls the subject over from the adjoining room, points to a bundle of carrots and a small stack of plastic containers on the table, and says they need them put carefully into the bag. The subject steps up to the chair, lifts the carrots with both hands, and lowers them into the bag, then places the containers on top one by one, adjusting them so the lid of each faces upward. The caregiver watches, nods once, pulls the bag’s handles together, and sets the packed bag by the door, ready to take out of the apartment.

On a cool mid-afternoon, the caregiver and the subject walk into the municipal culture house and approach a low shelf where several children’s books are displayed with their covers facing out. The caregiver exchanges a few words with a staff person at a nearby desk, then gestures toward the shelf and tells the subject they can pick one book to look at while they wait. The subject slowly runs a hand along the row of thin, colorful volumes, pauses at a book with a bright drawing of mountains and a small village on the cover, and pulls it out. The caregiver glances at the cover, nods, and leads the way to a wooden table with two chairs. They sit side by side, and the subject lays the chosen book flat on the table and opens it to the first page while the other books remain on the shelf behind them.

intellectualEncounter.subjectLabel: children’s picture book about an Andean village

episode.observableAction: Early evening in the apartment, the subject sits at the small table with a sheet of lined notebook paper and a worn blue pen, slowly copying a short paragraph of Spanish homework from the open textbook. The caregiver, standing nearby with a dish towel over one shoulder after finishing the dishes, leans down to glance at the page. Without asking anything, the caregiver reaches over the subject’s hand, takes the pen, and quickly crosses out a misspelled word in the middle of a sentence, rewriting it correctly above the line. The caregiver adds a small accent mark on another word, taps the corrected sentence once with the tip of the pen, and sets the pen back on the table before turning toward the sink again, while the subject remains seated with the partially completed homework in front of them.

Mid-afternoon in a bright classroom at the public secondary school, the subject sits at a shared wooden desk near the middle of the room while a science teacher stands at the front beside a small table. On the table, the teacher has set up a clear plastic bottle half-filled with water, a narrow glass tube, and a rubber balloon stretched over the bottle’s mouth. After briefly heating the bottle by placing it in a basin of warm water, the teacher lifts it out so everyone can see the balloon slowly inflate. Several students lean forward, murmuring. The teacher explains that the air inside the bottle expands when it gets warmer and pushes into the balloon. The subject watches the balloon swell, then raises a hand. When the teacher nods toward them, the subject asks aloud whether the balloon would shrink again if the bottle were put into cold water instead. The teacher pauses, smiles slightly, and says they will test that next, turning back to the table to prepare a second basin with cooler water while the subject continues watching from their desk.

intellectualEncounter.subjectLabel: Air expands when heated and contracts when cooled, affecting the volume inside a container and inflating or deflating a balloon.

episode.observableAction: On a cool Saturday afternoon at the municipal culture house, the subject walks alone into the small library room and stops in front of a low shelf where several thin books and magazines are arranged with their covers facing out. A staff person wearing a plastic name badge, seated behind a nearby desk, looks up and tells the subject they can choose something to read while the reading room is open. The subject nods without replying, then slowly scans the row of covers: one shows a cartoon character with speech bubbles, another has a photograph of a soccer team, and another displays a color photograph of Machu Picchu with a bold title about the history of the Incas. The subject reaches first toward the magazine with the soccer team, hesitates with fingers resting on the edge, then draws that hand back and instead grips the booklet with the Machu Picchu cover, sliding it off the shelf. Holding the booklet in one hand, the subject walks to an empty wooden table, pulls out a chair, sits down, and opens the booklet to the first page while the staff person returns to sorting a small stack of returned books at the desk.

intellectualEncounter.subjectLabel: Spanish-language booklet on Machu Picchu and Inca history

episode.observableAction: In a bright late-morning secondary school classroom, the science teacher distributes optional free Saturday robotics workshop registration forms, placing two on the subject’s shared desk, after which the peer pushes their blank form aside saying they prefer soccer, while the subject reads their own form, takes a pen from their backpack, fills in their name and section, walks to the front to place the completed form on the teacher’s desk, and then returns to sit beside the same peer.

intellectualEncounter.subjectLabel: photocopied registration form for optional Saturday robotics workshop

episode.observableAction: In a late-morning secondary school science class, the teacher writes "Los metales se dilatan con el calor" on the board and explains that heated metal expands, the subject asks if this explains why electric cables between posts look tighter or looser, then uses a piece of string with the teacher’s help to compare the circumference of a cool desk leg with that of a sunlit desk leg near the window, and finally reports that any difference is too small to detect with the string before returning to their seat.

intellectualEncounter.subjectLabel: thermal expansion of metals

episode.observableAction: On a cool late afternoon in the municipal culture house reading room, the subject walks in carrying a worn school backpack and stops at a shelf where several thin paperbacks and magazines are arranged with their covers facing out. One booklet shows a cartoon superhero, another has a large photograph of Machu Picchu with a title about Inca engineering, and a third displays a cross on a hillside with the Spanish title "¿Qué es la fe?" in bold letters. The librarian at the nearby desk looks up from a stack of forms and says the room will close in about an hour and that the subject can choose something to read. The subject glances briefly at the superhero cover, then at the Machu Picchu booklet, and finally reaches toward the booklet with the cross, sliding it off the shelf. Holding it in one hand, the subject walks to an empty wooden table, sets the backpack down by the chair, sits, and opens the booklet near the middle where a heading reads "La fe es confiar en lo que no vemos" above a short paragraph of text, while the librarian returns to stamping due-date slips at the desk.

intellectualEncounter.subjectLabel: Spanish-language booklet "¿Qué es la fe?" explaining a definition of faith

The subject stands near a low wall with a plastic folder under one arm when cousin_1 walks over, bouncing a worn rubber ball in one hand, and says they are going to play a quick game on the far side of the courtyard. Cousin_2, already a few steps away, turns and waves the subject over, calling out that they need one more person. The subject, seated beside them, keeps their own form in front of them, reads the printed description of building small vehicles with motors, and then reaches into their backpack for a pen. While the peer leans back in their chair and starts talking across the aisle about a weekend match, the subject bends over the paper and writes their full name and section in the spaces provided, then stands up, walks to the front, and places the completed form on the teacher’s desk before returning to sit again next to the same peer.
